title: "Use a checked data file in a test"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
description: >
  Create a small fixture, check its identity, and share package data between
  ordinary and long tests.
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Use a checked data file in a test}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
---

```{r fixture-options, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE)
```

A fixture is input data kept for a repeatable test. This recipe uses a tiny
table of sample counts. We will run a case, change the file, and see the
runner refuse to use the changed input.

Use the [GitHub development build](https://github.com/xec-cm/biocroxytest/tree/devel)
and the dependencies from [the first tutorial](biocroxytest.html). The
example package already lists `fs` in `Suggests`; add it to your own
package when declaring file fixtures. Run the following blocks in order.

## Create the input file

Start with a fresh copy of the example package. The temporary `pkg`
directory belongs to this recipe and can be deleted afterwards.

```{r fixture-package}
template <- system.file("examples", "samplealignment", package = "biocroxytest", mustWork = TRUE)
pkg <- tempfile("samplealignment-")
fs::dir_copy(template, pkg)
fixture <- file.path(pkg, "tests", "testthat", "counts.tsv")
contents <- "sample\tcount\ns1\t11\ns2\t21\ns3\t31\n"
writeBin(charToRaw(contents), fixture)
unname(tools::md5sum(fixture))
```

The checksum is `7f769a11cbd3fb2e9ad69db2f5d188a6`. It identifies the exact
file bytes, including line endings. `writeBin()` makes this example use
the same LF endings on every platform. For your own file, use the checksum
returned by `tools::md5sum()`.

## Declare and read the fixture

Replace `R/align-samples.R` **inside `pkg`** with the complete block below.
`source` is relative to `tests/testthat`, the directory of this case's
suite. The setup reads the verified path and constructs `x` before the
shared assertions run.

```{r fixture-source, eval=FALSE}
#' Select samples in the requested order
#'
#' @param x An object with named sample columns.
#' @param samples Sample names in the desired order.
#' @return The selected columns.
#' @export
#' @testCases sample-counts
#' list(
#'   cases = list(file = list(
#'     suite = "tests",
#'     fixtures = list(counts = list(
#'       source = "counts.tsv", md5 = "7f769a11cbd3fb2e9ad69db2f5d188a6"
#'     )),
#'     setup = {
#'       table <- read.delim(fixture_paths[["counts"]])
#'       x <- matrix(table$count, nrow = 1L,
#'                   dimnames = list("gene1", table$sample))
#'     }
#'   )),
#'   test = {
#'     selected <- align_samples(x, c("s3", "s1"))
#'     expect_identical(colnames(selected), c("s3", "s1"))
#'     expect_identical(as.integer(selected), c(31L, 11L))
#'   }
#' )
align_samples <- function(x, samples) x[, samples, drop = FALSE]
```

```{r write-fixture-source, include=FALSE}
writeLines(knitr::knit_code$get("fixture-source"), file.path(pkg, "R", "align-samples.R"))
```

Generate the test and run the named case. The case should be `completed`
and its file should be `verified`.

```{r verified-fixture, message=FALSE}
roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg)
id <- "sample-counts/file"
report <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(pkg, ids = id)
biocroxytest::check_test_plan(report, required = id)
report$cases[c("id", "status")]
report$fixtures[[id]][c("source", "status", "observed_md5")]
```

## See what happens when the file changes

Change the last count without changing the declaration. The named runner
checks fixtures before executing the case, so this run is `incomplete`,
with a fixture status of `mismatch`. The test body has not run.

```{r changed-fixture}
writeBin(charToRaw(sub("s3\t31", "s3\t99", contents, fixed = TRUE)), fixture)
changed <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(pkg, ids = id)
changed$cases[c("id", "status")]
changed$fixtures[[id]][c("source", "status")]
stopifnot(changed$cases$status == "incomplete",
          changed$fixtures[[id]]$status == "mismatch")
```

Restore the intended bytes and confirm the case completes again. Update
the declared checksum only when a fixture change is intentional and the
test's expected result has been reviewed.

```{r restore-fixture}
writeBin(charToRaw(contents), fixture)
restored <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(pkg, ids = id)
biocroxytest::check_test_plan(restored, required = id)
```

## Share a small file between both suites

A file needed by ordinary and long tests can instead live in
`inst/extdata`. Create a file containing the expected selected counts:

```{r shared-file}
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "inst", "extdata"), recursive = TRUE)
expected_file <- file.path(pkg, "inst", "extdata", "expected.txt")
writeBin(charToRaw("31\n11\n"), expected_file)
unname(tools::md5sum(expected_file))
withr::with_dir(pkg, biocroxytest::use_longtests())
```

Create `R/shared-counts.R` in `pkg` with this block. `fs::path_package()`
finds the file in a source package loaded for development and in an
installed package. The installed path starts at `extdata`, without `inst`.

```{r shared-source, eval=FALSE}
#' Shared expected counts
#' @noRd
#' @testCases shared-counts
#' list(
#'   cases = list(ordinary = list(suite = "tests"),
#'                long = list(suite = "longtests")),
#'   test = {
#'     file <- fs::path_package("samplealignment", "extdata", "expected.txt")
#'     expect_identical(unname(tools::md5sum(file)), "169ee1004dafb0ff3e7f141113e6f188")
#'     expected <- scan(file, what = integer(), quiet = TRUE)
#'     expect_identical(expected, c(31L, 11L))
#'     selected <- align_samples(example_experiment(), c("s3", "s1"))
#'     expect_identical(as.integer(SummarizedExperiment::assay(selected)), expected)
#'   }
#' )
NULL
```

```{r write-shared-source, include=FALSE}
writeLines(knitr::knit_code$get("shared-source"), file.path(pkg, "R", "shared-counts.R"))
```

```{r run-shared-file, message=FALSE}
roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg)
ids <- c("shared-counts/ordinary", "shared-counts/long")
shared <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(pkg, ids = ids)
biocroxytest::check_test_plan(shared, required = ids)
shared$cases[c("id", "suite", "status")]
```

Both rows should be `completed`. Here the checksum is an ordinary test
assertion. It is not a declaration in `fixtures`, so it does not add a
fixture-verification row to the report. Retained files under `inst` still
contribute to the source fingerprint recorded for the run.

## Remote and optional inputs

For an HTTPS fixture, use its URL as `source` and the checksum of the
intended file as `md5`. Install BiocFileCache and explicitly allow downloads
with `run_test_plan(pkg, download_fixtures = TRUE)`. Later runs can reuse
the verified cache offline; a custom `fixture_cache` must be outside `pkg`.
Planning and generation do not download files.

Standard testthat runs verify local declared fixtures and skip cases
requiring remote fixtures. The named runners resolve both kinds before
execution. Set `required = FALSE` only when the test handles an unavailable
input: its `fixture_paths` entry will be `NA_character_`.

```{r cleanup-fixtures, include=FALSE}
if ("samplealignment" %in% loadedNamespaces()) unloadNamespace("samplealignment")
unlink(pkg, recursive = TRUE)
```
